source_lines.76: 2.1 Expanding the finite sum from step 1.2 and using $\sum_i a_i=0$ yields $$\begin{aligned} \sum_{i,j}a_i a_j\gamma(s_i-s_j) &=\frac12\sum_{i,j}a_i a_j\mathbb E[Y_i^2+Y_j^2-2Y_iY_j]\\ &=-\mathbb E\!\left[\left(\sum_i a_iY_i\right)^2\right]\le0. \end{aligned}$$ The two sums containing $Y_i^2$ or $Y_j^2$ vanish because each contains the factor $\sum_i a_i$; the remaining term is the negative expectation of a square. No choice principle is used. [step 1.2, given, algebra] ∎

source_lines.64: 1.2 Define on the product of location and configuration spaces $$h(x,\mu)=\begin{cases}\mathbf1_Q(x)\bigl(\mu(D)-\mathbf1_D(0)\bigr),&\mu(\{0\})\ge1,\\0,&\mu(\{0\})=0.\end{cases}$$ This is nonnegative and product measurable: the two cases are measurable by the configuration evaluation sigma-algebra, and on the first case $\mu-\delta_0$ is a counting measure. For every counted occurrence $x=X_i$, [F2] puts $\theta_x\eta$ in the first case, and $h(x,\theta_x\eta)=\mathbf1_Q(x)(\theta_x\eta-\delta_0)(D)$. [F2, F3, F4, construct]
